A company is developing a SaaS solution for its customers. The solution runs on Amazon EC2 instances with attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Customers can request the amount of storage they need, and the application must allocate that amount of block storage to each customer. A solutions architect must design an operationally efficient solution that meets the storage scaling requirements. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
Migrate the data from the EBS volumes to Amazon S3 buckets. Use the S3 Standard storage class.

Migrate the data from the EBS volumes to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Use the EFS Standard storage class. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to increase EFS capacity based on user input.
Migrate the data from the EBS volumes to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to increase the file system's capacity based on user input.
Invoke an AWS Lambda function to increase the EBS volume size based on user input by using EBS Elastic Volumes.

A company is building a serverless application that processes large amounts of data from a mobile application. The application uses AWS Lambda functions to process the data and stores it in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company must ensure that the application can recover from failures and continue processing without losing any records. Which solution meets these requirements?

Configure the Lambda functions with an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue. Configure Lambda to retry failed records from the dead-letter queue. Implement an exponential backoff algorithm for retries.
Configure the Lambda functions to read records from Amazon Data Firehose. Replay the Firehose records if a failure occurs.
Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to store failed records. Configure AWS Lambda to retry the failed records from OpenSearch Service. Use Amazon EventBridge to coordinate the retry logic.
Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to store failed records. Configure Lambda to retry failed records from the SNS topic. Use Amazon API Gateway to coordinate the retry invocations.

A company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company hosts its website both on premises and in the AWS Cloud. Its on-premises data center is near us-west-1, and its AWS-hosted website is in eu-central-1. The company wants to optimize website load times as much as possible. Which solution meets these requirements?
Create a DNS record with a failover routing policy that routes all primary traffic to eu-central-1. Configure the on-premises data center as the secondary location.

Create a DNS record with an IP-based routing policy. Configure specific IP ranges to return the value for the eu-central-1 website. Configure all other IP ranges to return the value for the on-premises website.
Create a DNS record with a latency-based routing policy. Associate the record for the on-premises data center with us-west-1.
Create a DNS record with a weighted routing policy. Distribute traffic equally between eu-central-1 and the on-premises data center.

A healthcare company is designing a system to store and manage logs in the AWS Cloud. The system will receive and store logs in JSON format. The logs contain sensitive patient information. The company must identify sensitive data and be able to search the log data with SQL queries. Which solution meets these requirements?
Store the logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon Macie to discover sensitive data. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs.
Store the logs on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Create an application that uses Amazon SageMaker AI to detect sensitive data. Use Amazon RDS to query the logs.
Store the logs in Amazon DynamoDB. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to discover sensitive data. Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query the logs.
Store the logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Inspector to discover sensitive data. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs.

A company is developing a new web application that serves static and dynamic content through an API. The company wants to minimize latency for users accessing the application from around the world. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

Deploy the static content to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API to serve dynamic content. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket and HTTP API as origins. Enable caching for static content.
Deploy the static content to an Amazon S3 bucket. Give users the bucket's website endpoint. Use an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API with caching enabled to serve dynamic content.

Deploy the static content to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use two Amazon EC2 instances as web servers. Deploy an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket to cache static content.
Deploy the static content to an Amazon S3 bucket. Give users the bucket's website endpoint. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket to cache static content.

A company plans to deploy a managed MySQL database solution for a non-production application. The company plans to run the system on AWS for several years. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
Create an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Purchase a Reserved Instance.
Create an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Use On-Demand pricing.
Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster with a writer node and a reader node. Use On-Demand pricing for the cluster.
Create an Amazon EC2 instance. Manually install and configure MySQL Server on the instance.

A company is concerned about its Amazon RDS database. The workload is unpredictable, and periodic spikes in new user registrations could cause the company to run out of storage. The database runs on a general purpose instance with 300 GiB of storage. What should a solutions architect recommend?
Enable RDS storage autoscaling.
Schedule vertical instance scaling.
Change the database to a storage optimized instance type and vertically scale the database.
Configure an AWS Lambda function to increase RDS storage by 1 GiB when storage runs low.

A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances running Amazon Linux. The instances are behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and belong to an Auto Scaling group. Each instance uses an Amazon EBS volume to store product manuals. New instances often have outdated data and can take up to 30 minutes to receive updates from an external source. The company must ensure that all instances have the latest product manuals. The solution must adapt quickly to growing demand without changes to the application code. Which solution meets these requirements?
Store the product manuals on instance store volumes attached to each EC2 instance.
Store the product manuals in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the EC2 instances to download updates from the S3 bucket.
Store the product manuals on an Amazon EFS volume. Mount the EFS volume on the EC2 instances.
Store the product manuals in an Amazon S3 bucket using the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Configure the EC2 instances to download updates from the S3 bucket.

A company wants to deploy its containerized application at scale. The company also wants to adopt software solutions from the Kubernetes open-source community. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Deploy the application on an Amazon EKS cluster. Use EKS managed node groups with Amazon EC2 instances.
Deploy the application on an Amazon EKS cluster. Use EKS Auto Mode.
Run the application on a self-managed Kubernetes cluster running on Amazon EC2 instances.
Run the containerized application as an AWS Lambda function.

A company is developing a mobile financial application that allows users to register and store personal information. The application stores user information and preferences in an Amazon DynamoDB table and uses the data to generate credit score reports. The application sends users a credit report once a month. The company must give users the option to delete their data and preferences. The application must delete customer data within one month of receiving a deletion request. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Create an AWS Lambda function to delete user information. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs when the specified TTL expires. Configure the rule to invoke the Lambda function.

Create a DynamoDB stream. Create an AWS Lambda function to delete user information. Write user information from the DynamoDB table to the stream when the specified TTL expires. Configure the stream to invoke the function to delete the user information.

Enable TTL in DynamoDB. Store the expiration date as an attribute. Create an AWS Lambda function that sets the TTL based on the expiration date. Invoke the function when a user requests deletion of personal data.
Enable TTL in DynamoDB. Create an AWS Lambda function to delete user information. Configure AWS Config to detect changes in DynamoDB when the TTL expires and invoke the function.

A global company operates in multiple AWS Regions to meet data residency requirements. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage accounts. The company wants to restrict IAM roles to specific Regions to prevent unintended data operations across geographic boundaries. Which solution meets these requirements?
Configure a service control policy (SCP) that denies ec2:RunInstances in noncompliant Regions.
Configure IAM policies using the aws:RequestedRegion condition.
Configure IAM role trust policies using the aws:SourceIp condition.
Configure AWS Config to detect unwanted cross-Region access.
A data science workload needs storage for nightly log processing. The size and number of logs are unknown, and the logs are retained for only 24 hours. What is the MOST cost-effective solution?
Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
Amazon S3 Standard
Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering
Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)

An insurance company is developing an application to record individual user data, including names, ages, and health conditions. The company wants to run the application in private subnets on AWS. Data security requirements mandate access to the operating system of the compute resources running the application tier. The company must use a low-latency NoSQL database to store the data. Which solution meets these requirements?

Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application tier and Amazon DynamoDB tables for the database tier. Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB. Assign the instances an instance profile that allows access to DynamoDB.
Use AWS Lambda functions for the application tier and Amazon DynamoDB tables for the database tier. Assign the Lambda functions an appropriate IAM role to access the tables.
Use AWS Fargate for the application tier. Create an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL instance in private subnets for the database tier.
Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application tier. Store data in JSON format in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the application to use Amazon Athena to read and write data in the S3 bucket.

A company stores a file in Amazon S3. The file contains IP addresses and must be readable by the company's firewalls, which are not deployed on AWS. The company wants to restrict file access to the firewalls' IP addresses. Amazon S3 Block Public Access is configured for the AWS account. Which solution meets these requirements?
Configure the S3 bucket as a static website. Create a bucket policy that restricts website access to the firewalls' IP addresses. Add the static website URL to the firewall settings.
Create a bucket policy that explicitly allows access only from the firewalls' IP addresses. Add the file URL to the firewall settings.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as an origin. Create an origin access control (OAC) that allows access only from the firewalls' IP addresses.

Create an AWS Lambda function that can access the file. Configure the function to verify that a request's IP address belongs to one of the firewalls and return the list. Add the Lambda function URL to the firewall settings.

A company is developing an application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The company plans to make regular schema changes to test new features. Testing must not affect the existing production database. After testing, developers need to apply the changes to production. The solution must minimize downtime. Which solution meets these requirements?
Create a new temporary Aurora MySQL DB cluster based on the existing database. Make schema changes to the temporary cluster to test new features.
Create a read replica of the existing Aurora MySQL database. Make schema changes to the read replica. After successful testing, promote the read replica to the primary instance.

Create a blue/green deployment for the Aurora MySQL database. Make schema changes in the staging environment to test new features. After testing, direct traffic from the green environment to the blue environment.
Copy the Aurora MySQL database to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Make structural changes to the DynamoDB table to test new features. After testing, configure the application to use the DynamoDB table.

A solutions architect is building a static website to deploy on Amazon S3 for production. The website integrates with an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database through AWS Lambda functions. The production website uses a Lambda alias that points to a specific function version. The company must rotate database credentials every two weeks. Previously deployed Lambda functions must be able to use the latest credentials. Which solution meets these requirements?
Store the database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Enable rotation. Write code in the Lambda functions to retrieve credentials from Secrets Manager.
Include the database credentials in the Lambda function code. Update the credentials regularly and deploy new Lambda functions.
Use Lambda environment variables. Update the environment variables when new credentials become available.
Store the database credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Enable rotation. Write code in the Lambda functions to retrieve credentials from Parameter Store.

A company wants to use AWS Systems Manager to manage a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. Security requirements prohibit all EC2 instances from accessing the internet. A solutions architect must design network connectivity between the EC2 instances and Systems Manager while meeting this requirement. Which solution meets these requirements?
Deploy the EC2 instances in a private subnet with no route to the internet.
Configure an interface VPC endpoint for Systems Manager. Update routing to use the endpoint.
Deploy a NAT gateway in a public subnet. Configure the private subnet with a default route to the NAT gateway.
Deploy an internet gateway. Configure network ACLs to deny traffic to all destinations except Systems Manager.

A retail company stores customer behavior and session activity in Amazon DynamoDB. The company wants to run SQL queries in Amazon Redshift to track customer trends with regular updates. The company needs to automatically replicate data to Amazon Redshift without developing or managing extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Use AWS Glue to run scheduled ETL jobs that extract data from DynamoDB and load it into Amazon Redshift.
Use DynamoDB Streams with AWS Lambda functions to send near-real-time updates to Amazon Redshift.
Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query data exported from DynamoDB to Amazon S3.
Create a zero-ETL integration between DynamoDB and Amazon Redshift.

A global ecommerce company is designing a three-tier application on AWS. The web tier serves static content, the application tier handles business logic, and the database tier stores product information and user data. The application interacts with a relational database. The company needs a highly available architecture that serves global users with low latency. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups for both the web tier and application tier in the same AWS Region. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute web traffic. Use an Amazon RDS database with a Multi-AZ deployment for the database tier.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as its origin. Deploy the application tier in every AWS Region where the company operates, using Amazon ECS containers on AWS Fargate. Use an Amazon Aurora global database for the database tier.

Use an Amazon S3 bucket for static web content. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling and EC2 Spot Instances for the application tier. Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with read replicas for the database tier. Use AWS DMS to replicate data to a secondary AWS Region.

Use an Amazon S3 bucket for static web content. Use AWS Lambda functions for serverless backend logic in the application tier. Use Amazon API Gateway to invoke the functions to handle web requests. Use Amazon DynamoDB for the database tier and deploy it across multiple AWS Regions.

A solutions architect designs an application that allows users to access images stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses Amazon EC2 instances in a private VPC with the ID vpc-11aabb22. The solutions architect enables S3 Block Public Access on the bucket. The bucket is in us-west-2 in account 123456789012. Only resources in the VPC hosting the EC2 instances must be able to access the S3 bucket. Which solution meets this requirement?
Create an S3 bucket policy statement with a Deny effect and the condition "StringNotEquals": {"aws:SourceVpc": "vpc-11aabb22"}.
Create an S3 bucket policy statement with an Allow effect and a Resource of "arn:aws:ec2:us-west-2:123456789012:vpc/vpc-11aabb22".
Create an S3 bucket policy statement with an Allow effect and the condition "StringNotEquals": {"aws:SourceVpc": "vpc-11aabb22"}.
Create an S3 bucket policy statement with a Deny effect and the condition "StringNotEquals": {"aws:PrincipalAccount": "123456789012"}.
